C1 ruling: criterion 7 can be read to demand the outcomes, so no requirement edit is needed (details below). Three non-blocking notes (H2, H3, O1) are for ORCH, the design and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR; H1 from round 4 is unchanged. Design may align to the amended text.

EVERY HUNK ACCOUNTED FOR
Reference: my round-4 copy of the file (0ee2858f..., the text I passed). In it, REQ-001 is d0641025... and REQ-007 is b0a739b4.... The analyst's before-copy (4450091a...), with status restored, reproduces both hashes. So between round 4 and the analyst's start only the status lines changed.
- REQ-001, 4 hunks:
  (1) status line pending -> in_progress. This is ORCH's, not part of the edit.
  (2) «Сбои»: one sentence about the main-session row (C2).
  (3) «Что меняется в проекте»: the tests sentence names the helper (C3).
  (4) AC6: two clauses in (г) and one scenario in «Проверка:» (C2).
  Parsed comparison: id, title, owner, depends_on and original_request are the same; the criteria are 14 -> 14 and only AC6 differs.

C2 RESOLVED
- The text of (г) is testable, consistent with (в) and the rest of criterion 6, with criteria 3-5 and 7, with decisions/0003 and with R2. «окончание не записано» for a row whose end was not seen is a true statement, not an invented event. The «Проверка:» names a runnable page-test scenario: request, then server start gives «окончание не записано», then end of answer gives «завершена».
- Own test. I wrote two independent implementations, without using the analyst's script:
  (i) the design's first-event rule from §4.2: the first of Stop, next request or session end decides; only if none exists does a server start with journal_lines > i close the row;
  (ii) an event-driven reading written from the criterion text only.
  I compared them on 15 hand-built journals and on every prefix of 6,000 random journals (two sessions, resumes, session ends, untrusted lines, 0-3 server starts at random positions): 57,117 comparisons, 0 differences.
- Hand-built cases that agree with the design:
  - a server start before the request leaves it «обрабатывает запрос»;
  - a Stop after a session end (with resume) leaves the row unrecorded, because the row is not «closed only by a server start»;
  - a Stop after a next request belongs to the next row;
  - a second Stop changes nothing;
  - a Stop of another session, an untrusted Stop and an untrusted request change nothing;
  - request, server start, next request gives unrecorded and then in progress.
- The text equals the design's rule at every point: §4.2 (the first-event rule and its box), §3.5 (closed_by "server_start"), §9.4 item 7 (README limitation 7), D9 option 2 and PG-12d6. The late-Stop sentence is the design's «самоисправление» and covers a restart during a running turn. Design snapshot read: docs/design/REQ-001-pixel-office.md v2, sha256 cb90e05f..., 2436 lines (the designer was editing it). Per its header, v2 keeps D9, §4.2 and PG-12d6 as in v1 until your PASS.
- Wrong readings measured against the design on the same prefixes (differing prefixes):
  - «server start closes for good»: 4,235. The named scenario kills it, because of the late Stop.
  - «any server start anywhere in the journal closes the row»: 9,500.
  - «a Stop of any session closes the row»: 8,362.
  - The last two are NOT decided by the single-session named scenario; see H2.

C3 RESOLVED. Scratch copy of the current tree (rsync without node_modules, npm ci). Baseline npm run check: exit 0, 115/115, skipped 0, todo 0.
- (a) npm test does not run the helper. I used a helper with a failing top-level test that also sets exit code 3: npm test exits 0, 115 tests, no mention of the helper. The script is `node --test "test/**/*.test.js"`.
- The existing tools/test/helpers.js follows the same convention. A bare `node --test` would run both helpers (exit 1, 3 and 2 mentions); the glob in the script is what prevents it, and nothing in the requirements invokes a bare node --test.
- (b) prettier and eslint cover it: a mis-formatted helper gives format:check exit 1; an unused variable gives lint exit 1.
- (c) AC14 pins with the helper present (24 files): rules 856ee001..., globals bec0f88d..., package pin 5c592925..., .prettierignore cd446cc5..., .gitignore 4d56952b..., find-config-path exit 1, skip/todo grep 1, word grep 1.
- (d) The Q6 directive grep over tools/src/pixel-office tools/test still decides. It exits 0 (found, so the check fails as intended) for `/* eslint no-undef: 0 */`, `/* eslint-disable */` and `// prettier-ignore` placed in the helper; it exits 1 on a clean helper.
- (e) Wording. «прежние тесты, в том числе tools/test/helpers.js, не меняются» and «только новые файлы» are kept in both write-set lists. The helper is inside tools/test/ of ORCH's declaration. The cited «строки 1 и 3» of parallel-runs.jsonl are still the PO lines; the ISS-0002 line 5 does not touch these paths. I checked all write-set paths of both requirements with snapshot-diff's allow rule: all allowed.

RULING ON C1 (poll protocol: timeout, one request in flight, `from` check)
Criterion 7, read together with criterion 5, can be read to demand the OUTCOMES of the design fix. No requirement edit is needed for the design fix to be binding.
- (a) Timeout: yes. «если сервер недоступен — пишет «Нет связи с сервером Pixel Office»». A server that accepts the connection and never answers is unavailable; criterion 10 already lists it separately for the hook («сервер завис»). I checked it on Node 22 against a listener that accepts and never answers: a plain fetch stayed pending for the whole 8 s with no failure; with AbortSignal.timeout(3000) it rejected after 3004 ms. Without a timeout the message can never appear, so the outcome is demanded. The number (3 s) is the design's choice.
- (b) One request in flight: not demanded by itself. It is a mechanism for (c).
- (c) `from` check: the outcome is demanded. After recovery the page's array must equal the server's journal, with no duplicates and no skipped lines: «догружает пропущенные события», criterion 5 (one array), and the index-based rules. The `from === entries.length` check is the mechanism.
The «Проверка:» names «обрыв и восстановление» with «поддельные часы и сеть», which is enough as an instrument: a never-settling fake fetch and a duplicated response.

NON-BLOCKING NOTES
H2 - REQ-001 criterion 6(г), «Проверка:» (Q5). The named scenario does not decide two wrong implementations: a server start counted regardless of order, and a Stop matched across sessions. The first is the serious one. The server's own start is always recorded, so a live turn would show «окончание не записано» from its first second and flip to «завершена» at its Stop, and every single-session fixture without a server start would still pass. Recommendation: carry both into the design's PG-12d6 and into TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's mutant list (like M18): «запрос после запуска сервера — строка «обрабатывает запрос»; конец ответа другой сессии строку не закрывает». If ORCH prefers it in the requirement, one phrase in (г)'s «Проверка:» (and «конец ответа той же сессии» in the late-Stop sentence). I did not make it blocking: the rule text already states the boundary («после её начала»; «той же сессии» for the next request), a test is derivable, and Q5 requires failure cases.
H3 - criterion 7 «Проверка:» (optional, from the C1 ruling). If ORCH wants the test obligation literal: «обрыв (в том числе запрос, который не завершается) и восстановление без дублей и пропусков». I would not spend a round on it; the design validator's PG-14b/c/d carry it.
O1 - REQ-007 AC2, pre-existing and unchanged. It never says when the «Основная сессия» character works. Design §4.5 uses «есть открытая строка основной сессии», so C2 reaches the office through the design. If ORCH wants it in the requirement, one clause in AC2: the character works while a main-session row is open (REQ-001 6(г)).
H1 from round 4 is unchanged (AC14 not touched this round) and still non-blocking.
